newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX power futures shed gains, PV closes up 6 cts.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX power futures shed gains, PV closes up 6 cts.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures fell back near the close with March Palo Verde (PV) going off the board at $14.49 per megawatt hour (MWh), up 6 cents after rising as high as 85 cents, traders said Tuesday.
The March California-Oregon border (COB) contract, which also expired, lost 13 cents to settle at $10.44 per MWh.
"PV had a big run on Monday. Some people got caught short and had to cover," said one dealer.
He expected PV trading volume to pick up speed over the next few weeks as market focus begins to shift to the Southwest.
NYMEX said an estimated 256 COB and 338 PV contracts traded on Tuesday.
The April PV contract, which has been boosted by the recent upward trend for March, was expected to see further gains, although not for the long-term.
"April has more to the upside--maybe 25 or 50 cents," said one trader.

But the start of warmer spring temperatures and the expected restart late next week of the 1,070 megawatt unit 2 at the San Onofre nuclear plant in southern California would limit any rally, traders said.
"I expect April (PV) to head back to the 12's" before expiry next month, said the first trader.
April COB settled unchanged at $9.95 a MWh, while May was flat at $10.00.
April and May PV gained 10 cents to settle at $13.10 and $14.00, respectively.

In the Pacific Northwest, temperatures were expected to be about three degrees Fahrenheit below normal in the north to nine degrees below normal in the southeast through much of the week. Some precipitation was seen likely mid-week.

In the Southwest, temperatures were expected to be two degrees below normal on the coast and five degrees below normal in east-central areas through much of the week, with some precipitation likely, especially in the south and east.
